# Revelation 7: verse-by-verse research notes

**What's missing:** I ran out of searches before reaching any Lutheran (lcms.org, 1517.org), Pentecostal denominational (ag.org, pneumareview.com), Orthodox (oca.org) or modern scholarship (bibleodyssey.org, netbible.org) pages. I also found nothing on prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace readings of this chapter. Those are left out rather than guessed. Enduring Word (David Guzik, Calvary Chapel) is the nearest thing here to a charismatic-leaning source.

**Chapter overview**
- The chapter is a pause between the sixth seal (6:12–17) and the seventh seal (8:1). This passage comes in an interlude between the judgment of the sixth seal of the tribulation (Revelation 6:12–17) and the opening of the seventh seal (Revelation 8:1). (https://www.gotquestions.org/144000.html)
- Mark Copeland suggests the two visions answer the question that ends chapter 6: "For the great day of His wrath has come, and who is able to stand?" (https://www.ccel.org/contrib/exec_outlines/rev/rev_07.htm)

---

**v. 1**
- Guzik says "four corners of the earth" is an old way of saying the four points of the compass, so these angels affect the whole earth. He reads the winds as a destructive force of God's judgment, as they often are in the Old Testament (e.g., Hosea 13:15). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/)
- He also suggests the four winds may point back to the four horsemen of 6:1–8, following Zechariah 6:1–8, where the Hebrew *ruach* can mean either "spirits" or "winds." (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/)
- Bible Hub's summary says this symbolizes a temporary pause in judgment, allowing for the sealing of God's servants. (https://biblehub.com/revelation/7.htm)

**v. 2**
- Guzik notes that seals were familiar in the ancient world. A king or property owner used one to show ownership or that something was genuine. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/)
- Bible Hub: the seal (Greek *sphragis*) signifies protection and ownership by God. (https://biblehub.com/revelation/7.htm)

**v. 3**
- Guzik says the seal on the forehead protects them and somehow carries God's name (14:1). He compares Ezekiel 9:4, where the righteous were marked before Jerusalem was judged. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/) An older edition of his study guide adds that the seal is the Hebrew letter *tau* ("t," as in the shape of a small cross). (https://blueletterbible.org/Comm/guzik_david/StudyGuide_Rev/Rev_7.cfm)
- Guzik's application: although the 144,000 are sealed for a unique purpose, every believer is sealed by the Holy Spirit at salvation (2 Cor. 1:21–22; Eph. 1:13; 4:30). That sealing is both a comfort (we belong to Him) and a challenge (turn from evil). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/)
- Reformed reading (Kevin DeYoung): Ezekiel 9's mark separated idolaters from non-idolaters, so the sealing of the 144,000 makes a similar distinction based on who worships God not who among the Jewish remnant worships God. (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/blogs/kevin-deyoung/who-are-the-144000-in-revelation/)
- Copeland (amillennial-style reading): the sealed church on earth is spared God's wrath, but while they may escape God's wrath they may still face the efforts of Satan (12:17; 13:7ff). (https://www.ccel.org/contrib/exec_outlines/rev/rev_07.htm)

**v. 4: who are the 144,000? (the main point where Protestants disagree)**
- **Dispensational/futurist view (Calvary Chapel, GotQuestions, bible.org, MacArthur):**
  - Guzik sees them as Jewish people who come to faith in Jesus and are protectively sealed through the tribulation. His reasons:
    - they are called "children of Israel";
    - their tribes are named;
    - they are celibate (14:4);
    - the New Testament never calls the church "Israel."
  
  He quotes Seiss calling them a "superaddition to the Church – a supplementary body". (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/)
  - GotQuestions takes them as a literal 144,000 Jews whom God protects so they can freely perform their mission during the tribulation. (https://www.gotquestions.org/144000.html)
  - Bible.org sees them as the great evangelists of the Tribulation period. (https://bible.org/seriespage/13-redeemed-tribulation-rev-71-17)
  - According to TGC, John MacArthur sees them as a "firstfruits of Israel," set apart "to proclaim the gospel" during the seven-year tribulation. (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/who-are-144000-revelation/)
- **Reformed view (TGC):**
  - DeYoung: The 144,000 represent the entire community of the redeemed. He explains the number as 12 × 12 × 1000, which is a way of saying all of God's people under the old and new covenant. (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/blogs/kevin-deyoung/who-are-the-144000-in-revelation/)
  - Benjamin Gladd reads verses 5–8 against the census in Numbers, so God, in other words, has assembled a messianic army. (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/who-are-144000-revelation/)
- **Older commentators:**
  - Gill treats 144,000 as 12 times 12,000. He takes it to mean those who are truly the spiritual offspring of the twelve apostles, holding their teaching.
  - Adam Clarke (Methodist) took the number to include all Jews converted to Christianity. He treated it as a definite number standing for an indefinite one, since exactly 12,000 per tribe is not to be supposed. (https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/amp/revelation/7-4.html)
  - The Pulpit Commentary notes that the actual act of sealing is not described, just as in Ezekiel 9. (https://biblehub.com/revelation/7-4.htm)
- **Other groups:** Jehovah's Witnesses take the number literally but the tribes symbolically, as "spiritual Jews" who rule in heaven. (https://www.gotquestions.org/Jehovahs-Witnesses-144000.html) Guzik notes that the Witnesses once said their entire group was, until they surpassed 144,000 in number. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/)

**vv. 5–8: the tribe list**
- Guzik's points:
  - Dan is left out. Some link Dan to the Antichrist, but Dan certainly brought idolatry into Israel. Dan is listed first in Ezekiel 48.
  - "Joseph" seems to stand for Ephraim, who may be slighted for idolatry (Hosea 4:17).
  - The list is not "irregular" proof of symbolism: the Old Testament lists the tribes about 20 different ways. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/)
- Gladd notes the unusual order: Judah appears at the top of the list in Relevation (he should be fourth). (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/who-are-144000-revelation/)
- DeYoung says the number, the list and the order are all stylized. He also notes that some non-biblical Jewish writings expected the Antichrist to come from Dan (Gen. 49:17). (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/blogs/kevin-deyoung/theological-primer-the-144000/)
- Copeland: Ephraim and Dan are missing while Levi and Joseph are counted, and this suggests to many that the 144,000 of Israel is symbolic. (https://www.ccel.org/contrib/exec_outlines/rev/rev_07.htm)
- Ellicott says the tribes are grouped in order of closest kinship. (https://biblehub.com/revelation/7-4.htm)

**v. 9**
- Guzik's points:
  - The diversity of the crowd shows the Great Commission will be fulfilled (Matt. 24:14).
  - Spurgeon is quoted to argue that individuality remains in heaven.
  - The white robes picture both Christ's covering righteousness and priestly service.
  - The palm branches recall the triumphal entry and stand for victory won through hardship. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/)
- Gill reads the white robes as fitting the saints' princely and priestly character. The Geneva Study Bible reads the scene as showing priests, kings and glorious conquerors by martyrdom. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/7-9.htm)
- **Who is the crowd? (another point of disagreement):**
  - Dispensational writers see tribulation converts, many of them martyrs. Bible.org: a great multitude of martyred dead in heaven. (https://bible.org/seriespage/7-saints-great-tribulation)
  - Copeland sees the church "triumphant," i.e., all the redeemed in heaven. (https://www.ccel.org/contrib/exec_outlines/rev/rev_07.htm)
- **Catholic:** Catholic Answers argues that nation, tribe and people mean nothing to angels, so John means humans. Therefore, souls continue to exist beyond death. (https://www.catholic.com/bible-navigator/immortality-of-the-soul/revelation79-10)

**v. 10**
- Guzik: the crowd recognises that God alone is the source of salvation. Having an emblem of righteousness (white robes), they worship God for salvation. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/)
- A Pulpit Commentary homily on Bible Hub: the redeemed give the credit for their redemption to God and the Lamb, and All is "of him." (https://biblehub.com/sermons/revelation/7-9.htm)

**vv. 11–12**
- Guzik: when the redeemed praise God, all the beings around the throne join in. Seeing the salvation God brought, they see His power and wisdom more clearly. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/)
- Copeland: the angels, elders and living creatures fall on their faces and offer seven words of praise. (https://www.ccel.org/contrib/exec_outlines/rev/rev_07.htm)

**v. 13**
- Guzik: John didn't know he should ask, so the elder prompted the question. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/)
- Bible Hub commentary: The question brings the white robes into prominence. (https://biblehub.com/revelation/7-13.htm)
- Bible.org argues that the elder's question shows the 24 elders are a different group from the crowd. (https://bible.org/seriespage/7-saints-great-tribulation)

**v. 14**
- **"The great tribulation":** Guzik says the definite article ("the") is emphatic, which leads many to see these as martyrs of the end-time tribulation. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-7/) Augustus Toplady (Anglican, on monergism.com) reads it more broadly, as trouble of every kind. Believers are tried by the world, outwardly; and, inwardly, by their own corruptions. (https://www.monergism.com/thoughts-revelation-71415) Matthew Henry: The way to heaven lies through many tribulations. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/7-14.html)
- **"Washed... in the blood":** Writers across traditions agree that the cleansing comes from Christ's blood, not from suffering.
  - Barnes says the robes are made white not by their sufferings or afflictions but by the Lamb's blood.
  - Gill rules out bulls' and goats' blood, their own suffering and their own works.
  - Constable: The blood of martyrs shed for the Lamb's sake would not even do it. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/7-14.html)
- **Different emphases on how the washing happens:**
  - Spurgeon (Baptist) stresses faith alone. They brought nothing but their filthy garments: They did not give, they took; they did not impart, but they received. In another sermon he rejects the idea that the tribulation helped purify them. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/7-14.html; https://www.spurgeon.org/resource-library/sermons/why-the-heavenly-robes-are-white/)
  - Adam Clarke (Wesleyan) says they obtained their *pardon* and *purity*, through the *blood of the Lamb*. Coffman (Restoration Movement, Arminian) treats "wash your robes" passages as stressing the human response in salvation. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/7-14.html)
  - A Bible Hub homily (preacher not named) notes that "they washed" implies something for them to do. It holds that the cleansing includes the making of a pure character, not mere forgiveness. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/7-9.htm)

**v. 15**
- Toplady: they are before the throne Not because they came out of great tribulation; but because they and their robes were washed. Matthew Poole says the same. (https://www.monergism.com/thoughts-revelation-71415; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/7-15.htm)
- Ellicott: The life is not simply one of joy or safety, it is one also of service. He notes the temple language must be figurative, since the heavenly city has no temple (21:22). (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/7-15.htm)
- John Wesley (Methodist): "day and night" means continually, and God Shall spread his glory over them as a covering. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/7-15.html)
- One Bible Hub homily links the palm branches and the "tabernacle" to the Feast of Tabernacles, as if the crowd were keeping that feast. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/7-15.htm)
- Constable (dispensational) says this is God's present heavenly sanctuary, not the new Jerusalem. Coffman stresses that God's sheltering love is available to His people now. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/7-15.html)

**v. 16**
- Barnes: few images of happiness would strike someone from the Middle East more than fountains in burning, sandy wastes. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/7-17.htm)
- Copeland ties these promises to the eternal state by comparing 7:16–17 with 21:1–4. (https://www.ccel.org/contrib/exec_outlines/rev/rev_07.htm)

**v. 17**
- Ellicott (Bible Hub): the Good Shepherd of Psalm 23 and John 10 does not forget the shepherd's work in heaven. (https://biblehub.com/revelation/7-17.htm)
- Another commentator on the same Bible Hub page says that anyone who would come near the throne must pass the Lamb. He also says the Isaiah 49 quotation is "elevated": the Lamb, not just "he that hath mercy," leads them, and to waters of *life*. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/7-17.htm)
- Barnes: "living" waters means the happiness will never end. The tears image comes from Isaiah 25:8. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/7-17.htm)
- Benson (Methodist) reads the living fountains as The comforts of the Holy Spirit. (https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/7-15.html)
- GotQuestions: the springs refer to eternal life found in Jesus. (https://www.gotquestions.org/springs-of-living-water.html)
- One older homily on Bible Hub warns: If all tears are to be wiped away hereafter, it follows that religion does not profess to wipe them away here. (https://biblehub.com/sermons/revelation/7-17.htm)
